annotationRationale: Bisecting diagonals identify the constructed parallelogram, whose equal opposite sides create an isosceles triangle. The midsegment theorem transfers its angle to MN; parallel-line properties and triangle angle sums supply the angle calculations.
sourceMethod: Followed the first official construction, extending PN to Q, forming parallelogram UPGQ, and using an isosceles triangle and a midsegment. Explained the construction and ray positions without relying on the official diagram.

review.mathCheck: The constructed diagonals bisect, giving \(GQ\parallel PT\) and \(GQ=AG\). The specified ray directions give \(\angle QGA=92^\circ\), so \(\angle QAG=44^\circ\). The side-of-line argument correctly yields \(\angle QAP=100^\circ\); the midsegment parallelism then gives the acute angle \(80^\circ\), choice E.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 23's first construction, page 14. The construction and angle placement agree with the supplied figure, and the candidate explicitly justifies the ray order needed for adding 44 degrees and 56 degrees.
